answer: An agent economy can make each identity post a refundable bond before it may bid, vote, or claim a reward. When an agent breaks a rule or fails a task, the protocol slashes that bond; creating a thousand sybils therefore requires locking a thousand bonds, not merely minting cheap accounts. The bond should be sized to the value an attack could capture, so coordinated identities face a real capital cost. An ivory token, pigment label, or oasis-themed profile adds no security unless backed by that same stake.
